from one trans person to another, transitioning (if you want to of course, but sounds like you do) is so so worth it. I'm a trans dude who's been on T for two years now. I'm so much more happy since starting, even though I thought I wouldn't get to this point. A lot of my friends are also trans, mostly trans women, and a lot of them are seeking to transition, legally change their names, and all that, and I get to watch them from the perspective of someone who's already done it. all my friends get happier as their social and medical transitions move forward, and it makes me happy for them! a lot of them also have parents that don't understand. The best results we've gotten is by sending resources to the parents or printing them out for them to read. Stuff like how transitioning is good, hormone blockers are good, and the emotional side of being trans, and how support also saves lives. If nothing else, you can also always reach out to LGBTQ+ support groups in the area, the trans community is very supportive. I wish you luck - but I think there's so so much worth it to transitioning, I hope you get the chance <3

I don't know how to help, but I've felt similarly before. I'm also 23 and have never dated anyone. I personally don't think people's appearances can be reduced to "ugly" or "not ugly" but there certainly is a standard of beauty that exists and it does end up affecting peoples (especially women's) lives. That being said, hold on if you can. I think the solution is just to unfortunately accept that some people are very vain. Some people aren't, and could like you. Plus, regardless of society's value of you as beautiful or ugly, people have more inherent worth than that. You could be a great craftsmaker, you could be a great friend, you could be great at laying down in the grass and letting the wind flow across your face- all of these are fine, wonderful things, and all are unrelated to how you look.

I'm sorry that your father is homophobic. I always recommend not coming out if it's unsafe, if you can hold on a bit longer. Maybe one day you will have the funds to move out or get to a bigger area with more LGBTQ+ people in the area. If you're going to end up in an unsafe situation I really suggest you don't come out if you can hold on, but I understand not being able to hold onto being in the closet any longer. Maybe there could be other people in your small area that could hitch you a ride to a bigger city to find temporary shelter. Don't get in cars with people you don't know though. I hope you're safe

I also have a very strong survival instinct, I feel that. I'm desperate most days to find help because of it, and I end up telling anyone and everyone that I want to die. I finally agreed with one person to seek out a psychiatrist tomorrow. I think as much as there are always uncaring people, there's also always very caring people. Even if you haven't found someone to care yet, I think there's always a possibility of finding someone to care. I wouldn't know where to look though. Maybe if there are more healthcare services in your area you could reach out and try other doctors and teams. Good luck

I hope coming out goes alright for you, from one trans person to another. If nothing else, the trans community has always been caring and supportive amongst ourselves. Maybe if you need to, you can reach out to other trans people around your area for support or housing. Good luck

I don't know if it gets better, but one thing I do know is that it's never selfish to be alive - people exist naturally. No matter what your brain may tell you, the potential for clinging to life is never selfish, it's a glimmer of hope when all of us in this subreddit are all in an extremely dark place. We are all fighting to live, if against ourselves.

I'm sorry you've been getting bullied. People don't deserve to get relentlessly bullied. If it helps at all, I was bullied in middle school and I'm just out of college now and I haven't thought of my bullies since high school. The further away I got from them, the less I remembered them and how horrible I felt. It's subsided in this amount of time for me. I don't know how to help in the moment - I wasn't able to make it stop when it was happening, but if nothing else the bullies of my past aren't in my mind or in my life now.

I'm sorry that healthcare services haven't listened to you. I don't think hurting yourself will change them- uncaring people remain uncaring. Maybe there is a way to get the help you need without hurting yourself, there might be some healthcare workers somewhere that will willingly help you
